output.myth: Tirun came home keel-up on a grey morning, with no crew in her and no oars shipped. The women of the north shore turned her with ropes and found her lamps still burning under the thwarts, though the seal oil should have run dry a month before. Nobody had seen her leave. Tavo the Gale had been out that week, laughing at the boats, and he would not say what he had done. Ennu sat on the stones and cut the sailcloth open to see what she was made of, and found only salt and bone. Hesk counted the lamps and came up one short of the crew. So the lamps still burn under her, for every one who went out past the Leeward edge and did not come back. When you go out, hang a lamp under your own hull. If it is still lit when you return, somebody is waiting for you.
output.verse:
Come home keel-up, lamps
still lit beneath the wet boards,
no crew to say why.
